desc:
Shopify sales reports in plain English turn your store numbers into a short document that tells you what happened and what to do next. Ecom Swift LLC reads your own Shopify analytics and explains sales, products, customers and traffic in simple words.

## What is a Shopify sales report?

A Shopify sales report is a summary of how your store performed over a set period. It brings together orders, sales, average order value, product performance, customer behavior and traffic sources, and explains each one in a sentence.

Shopify already has many reports, but a screen full of charts does not tell you what to change. Our report does the reading for you, and ends with three clear actions.

## Why shop owners struggle with their numbers

Most owners look at one figure, usually total sales, and miss everything around it. They do not see which products sell and which sit idle, whether customers return, or which discount codes brought in good orders and which only cut margin.

The data is also spread across places. Orders live in one report, traffic in another, and discount results in a third. Putting the pieces together takes time that busy owners do not have, so decisions get made by feel.

## How clear reports improve decisions

A good report links cause and effect. If sales rose in a month, it shows whether the cause was more visitors, more orders from existing customers or larger baskets. If they fell, it shows where the drop began. That tells you whether to fix traffic, product pages or pricing.

Product views help with stock and promotion. Top products deserve space on the home page and enough inventory, while slow products may need better photos, a lower price, a bundle or removal. Customer views show whether you rely on one-time buyers or have a base that returns. We do not predict future results, because the report describes what already happened.

## What a useful report includes

- Total sales, number of orders and average order value for the period.
- A comparison with an earlier period, where your package includes one.
- Top selling products, and the slowest sellers.
- Traffic sources, such as search, social, email and direct.
- The split between new and returning customers.
- Discount code use and how those orders compare with full-price orders.
- Collection and product type breakdowns for larger packages.
- A sentence under every chart that explains what it shows.
- Three suggested actions, each tied to a number in the report.
- A PDF to read and a spreadsheet you can reuse.

## What we do

We work from your own Shopify analytics and order data, so nothing is estimated or invented. After you invite us as a staff or collaborator user with reporting permission, we export the data for the chosen period and check it for gaps.

Then we write the report in plain words. The Basic package covers one month with the key numbers and three actions. Standard compares two months and adds customers, discounts and a PDF with a sheet. Premium covers a quarter of trends, product and collection breakdowns, a dashboard sheet you can keep updating and a review call to walk through everything. If the data shows a problem, such as tracking that is switched off, we say so openly.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us which question you most want answered.
- Share any campaigns or events that ran during the period.
- Compare like with like, such as one month against the same kind of month.
- Pick one action from the report and finish it before choosing another.
- Keep the dashboard sheet updated each month.

**Avoid:**
- Judging the store from a single day or a single order.
- Comparing a sale month with a quiet month and reading it as a trend.
- Counting test orders and your own purchases as real sales.
- Changing five things at once, so you cannot tell what worked.
- Treating the report as a forecast.

## Who this is for

This service suits owners who open their analytics and close them again, unsure what they are looking at. It suits sellers preparing for a bigger push who want a starting point, and it suits teams who need a regular, readable summary to share with partners or an accountant.

## What we need from you

We need a staff or collaborator invitation with access to reports and orders, and the date range you want covered. We never need your password. We do not need access to payment details or card data. Tell us your goals and any events during the period, and we will send the report with a short note on how to read it.
